title: The Next Enlightenment Is Institutional
abstract: The Enlightenment was not an idea but an institutional build-out: learned societies, journals, correspondence networks, and constitutions that divided power so no single authority could recapture the verdict. Intelligence proliferation faces the same test. Kissinger argued in 2018 that intelligence systems mark how the Enlightenment ends, and he is correct about one scenario, the opaque and centralized one. The error is treating that scenario as the only one, because the Enlightenment never depended on every reader understanding Newton. It depended on institutions that made claims contestable. Mokyr's Republic of Letters was a non-transferable, domain-scoped, citation-weighted reputation system, a classification rather than an analogy. The institutional gap is measurable: across forty operational DAOs, agent alignment averages 2.10 of 10 and no DAO scores above 5. Three Enlightenment institutions translate directly. Separation of powers becomes separation of assessment, contestation and adjudication. The learned society becomes the staked validation pool. Constitutional amendment becomes dynamic regulation. The next Enlightenment will be measured by whether the institutions around the models keep reason contestable.

responds_to.name: Henry A. Kissinger, How the Enlightenment Ends, The Atlantic, June 2018
